correctness.rationale: Two identical source families in \(\mathbb R^2\) use \(K=I/2\), analysis operators \(P_{e_1},P_{e_2}\), unit weights and full fusion subspaces. Every undeleted weave has exact energy \(\|f\|^2\); \(A=B=3\) are legitimate, though not optimal, bounds because \(3\|K^*f\|^2=3\|f\|^2/4\le\|f\|^2\le3\|f\|^2\). Deleting index one costs \(C=2\), and \(\|K^\dagger\|^2=4\), so the printed condition \(2<12\) holds and incorrectly predicts lower constant one. The deleted weave is only \(P_{e_2}\) and vanishes at \(e_1\) while \(\|K^*e_1\|^2=1/4\). Fresh rational matrix arithmetic checked these identities. For the corrected theorem extend any deleted partition to all indices and subtract at most \(C\|f\|^2\); for \(f\in R(K)\), the closed-range estimate \(\|f\|\le\|K^\dagger\|\|K^*f\|\) gives the stated sufficient constant. The source proof itself contains this corrected factor in its last estimate.
correctness.risk: The corrected criterion is sufficient, not asserted necessary; coarse C may overestimate deleted energy.

value.rationale: A published stability theorem permits a stated sufficient condition that can falsely guarantee preservation of a positive lower frame bound; the explicit deletion destroys the frame. The scale-correct replacement and simple finite witness provide a motivated substantive correction relevant to perturbation/deletion applications.

final_claim: The sufficient deletion criterion \(C<A\|K^\dagger\|^2\) and lower bound \(A-C\) in Sadri--Rahimlou--Ahmadi Theorem 2.5 are false for woven \(K\)-\(g\)-fusion frames. A finite real two-dimensional weaving satisfies the printed assumptions yet deletion destroys the \(K\)-lower bound. The scale-correct sufficient criterion is \(C\|K^\dagger\|^2<A\) with lower bound \(A-C\|K^\dagger\|^2\) on \(R(K)\).
limitations: Corrected bound only sufficient, not necessary or optimal.
The false theorem is refuted for general closed-range K even with finite-dimensional identical families.
